findings.title: D6 would show "Findings Not Parsed" on reviews whose findings were parsed
findings.description:
D6 makes the `fallback_used` notice render "whenever `fallback_used` is set, after any findings". The same change goes into `_display_terminal`, and the `cli/commands/review.py` row at line 75 says the same thing. But `fallback_used=True` does not mean "findings not parsed". Slice 919's derived-verdict path sets `fallback_used=True` and `verdictSource: derived` precisely when findings *were* parsed and only the `## Summary` verdict was missing. Under D6, every derived-verdict review, capped or not, would print a "Findings Not Parsed" notice under its real findings. That contradicts the artifact and changes output outside this slice's scope.

The case D6 is meant to protect is "a PASS with `fallback_used=True`, verdict read, findings not". As far as I can tell, today's parser can't produce it. The findings-mismatch path only fires for CONCERNS/FAIL with no findings. The only PASS that can carry `fallback_used=True` is a derived one, and that always has findings.

Fix: either drop D6 and SC7 (line 292) as handling a case that doesn't exist, or base the notice on whether the model's own findings list was empty, ignoring the synthetic finding (for example, check before `impose_diff_coverage` prepends it). Then add a regression test that a derived-verdict review renders no notice.

findings.title: D9's id capture leaves out the `gemini` profile, which uses the OpenAI-compatible path
findings.description:
D9 (line 185) and the Risk section (lines 359-363) rely on walkthrough step 6 to collect each profile's real `answering_models` before merge, so the strict equivalence rule doesn't flag false substitutions. Step 6 lists sdk, openai, openrouter and local. `gemini` is also a built-in profile on the OpenAI provider type: Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, the same code path as D8's `chunk.model`. Slice 906 lists it in the six-profile matrix.

If Gemini returns a slightly different id form than the one requested, every Gemini review would write `requestedModel` and log a WARNING. That breaks the slice plan's Part C requirement that "an alias resolving to its own snapshot is not reported as a substitution" (`900-slices…md:443`). It also breaks D10's promise that `requestedModel` appearing means a real substitution.

Fix: add `gemini` to step 6 and to D9's list of profiles to capture. Also say what happens to a profile whose credentials aren't available at walkthrough time. It shouldn't silently go unchecked; record it as uncaptured in the DEVLOG.

findings.title: Handling of a missing `chunk.model` is assumed, not stated
findings.description: Line 58 treats `ChatCompletionChunk.model` as guaranteed on every chunk. The servers behind the `local` and `gemini` profiles are not OpenAI and may not follow that. D8 already handles an empty value ("last non-empty"), and D11 gives a well-defined "not reported" result for an empty list. One sentence would close the gap: an absent attribute counts the same as empty and leads to D11, never an exception. A stream cut off before the final Message is a provider failure, which D13 already covers.

findings.title: `aiModel` changes meaning in the cross-tool frontmatter contract
findings.description: Slice 911 calls review frontmatter a cross-tool contract with context-forge. D5 records a grep of context-forge for `verdictSource` readers, but nothing similar is recorded for `aiModel`. The design says its new meaning is "the meaning its consumers assumed all along" without that check. The metrology break for dated OpenAI judges is acknowledged at line 196. Recording a context-forge grep for `aiModel` would put the claim on the same footing as D5.
